Security admins can view database connection records using TLS 1.2 during business hours (9:00-18:00, Monday-Friday).
Security administrators can rotate gateway-managed API credentials only after the standard 90-day rotation interval has elapsed.
Security administrators can review password policy records that require passwords of at least 12 characters and remember at least 5 previous passwords.
Security administrators and auditors can view level 3 or higher privileged account records through multi-factor authentication.
Security administrators can review access session records where a 30-minute inactivity timeout is enforced.
Security administrators can update sensitive access operation records only when step-up verification was recorded within the last 5 minutes.
Security administrators can insert privilege escalation event records only with required and documented approval.
Security administrators can create temporary privileged access records only after approval and when an access duration is provided.
Security administrators can delete expired privileged access records.
Security administrators can view vault-stored secret items only when encryption is enabled.
Security administrators can update secret system configuration records when the secret has not been rotated for at least 30 days.
Security administrators can create hotfix code commit records only with a valid GPG signature.
Project owners or assigned reviewers can update project merge status, but a merge cannot be approved until it has at least two approvals.
Security administrators can update project code review records only when the updated review includes a security check.
Security administrators can create test results for package dependency changes only after the dependency scan has passed.
Security administrators can update container image test records only the updated record shows a passed vulnerability scan and approved deployment.
Security administrators can peer review infrastructure artifacts in the code repository only during maintenance windows (02:00-06:00), and the updated row must be marked as reviewed.
Security administrators can update network ACL configuration records only when the updated record is documented and approved.
Security administrators can view firewall configuration records reviewed within the last 90 days.
Security administrators and compliance officers can view VPN access records that meet the approved-device compliance requirement.
Security administrators can create remote session security event records only when logging and monitoring are both enabled.
Security administrators can view data-transfer access records that use TLS 1.3 encrypted channels.
Security administrators can update database replication access records only when SSL is enabled and the TLS version is at least 1.2.
Audit leads can view centralized, tamper protected security event records with immutability configured during business hours (09:00-18:00, Monday-Friday).
HR administrators can update active employee rows only inside the current tenant.
Managers may update attendance records only inside the current tenant and for rows in their department.
HR specialists may create benefit enrollment rows only for the active current tenant.
HR administrators may delete pending payroll approval rows only within their tenant.
Employees can update their own draft expense rows only inside the current tenant, and updated rows must remain owned by that employee in that tenant.
Finance managers may update current payroll rows only within their tenant, and updated rows must remain current in that tenant.
Finance analysts may insert revenue records only for the active current tenant.
Tax specialists may delete draft tax records only inside the current tenant.
Project owners can update draft engineering projects only in the current tenant, and updated project rows must remain draft projects owned by the same requester in that tenant.
Project managers may update issue rows whose current status is open or in-progress only within the current tenant, and updated rows must remain within that tenant.
Repository owners may create repository metadata only for themselves inside the current tenant.
DevOps engineers may delete failed build rows only within their tenant.
Compliance officers can review tenant audit logs from pending review to reviewed in their current tenant.
Security analysts can resolve unresolved security events only inside their tenant.
Operations managers may create documents only for the active current tenant.
SRE employees may perform all row-level operations on low-risk system configuration rows in their current tenant, and inserted or updated rows must remain low-risk and in that tenant.
IAM administrators may revoke expired access grant rows inside the current tenant only after the grant expires_at has passed; the updated row must be unapproved in that tenant.
Product managers can update active feature rows only inside the current tenant.
Product managers may update active metrics only within their tenant.
Data analysts may insert analytics rows only for the current tenant.
Roadmap owners may delete their own deferred roadmap items only within their tenant.
Customer support employees can escalate customer feedback assigned to them inside the current tenant; they may update only open feedback.
Account managers can update active customer rows assigned to them only inside the current tenant.
Account managers may update active contracts only within their tenant.
Sales representatives may create orders only for their tenant.
Finance managers may delete draft invoices only inside the current tenant.
Account managers can close pending customer communication records for accounts they manage inside the current tenant.
Account managers may update in-progress onboarding rows assigned to them only within their tenant.
Call center supervisors can update call recording rows only for their current tenant and team.
Call center supervisors may update recorded call recordings to reviewed only within their tenant.

Support operations employees can read customer rows in their own tenant. To read a customer from another tenant, they must have active, approved, unexpired break-glass read access granted to their application user account for that customer record.

Support operations employees can update contract rows in their own tenant. Cross-tenant contract updates require an active, approved emergency update access record granted to their application user account for the target tenant's contract records, and updated rows must stay within a permitted tenant.

Support operations employees can read expense rows in their own tenant. Cross-tenant expense reads require an active finance-review access record granted to their application user account for the target tenant that is still within its expiration time.

SRE employees can read engineering projects in their own tenant. Cross-tenant project reads require a project-specific temporal read access record granted to their application user account, from an approved device, with a completed step-up check in the last eight hours.

SRE employees can read audit logs in their own tenant. Cross-tenant audit log reads require an active, verified audit-read temporal access record granted to their application user account for the target tenant that has not expired.

SecOps responder employees can update security events in their own tenant. Cross-tenant event updates require a verified severity-matched update access record granted to their application user account, with real-time alerting enabled and a response SLA of at most 60 minutes, and the updated row must remain covered by the same rule.

Customer support employees can read product metrics in their own tenant. Cross-tenant metric reads require an active, minimum-necessary temporal access record granted to their application user account and scoped for the target tenant.

Data analysts can read analytics rows in their own tenant; analytics rows from another tenant require an approved, unexpired read grant issued to their application account for the row's tenant and a recorded approver.

Support operations employees can read call recordings in their own tenant; a recording from another tenant requires an approved, unexpired read grant issued to their application account for that tenant and targeting support call recordings.
HR administrators can read employee rows in their own tenant; employee rows from another tenant require a non-deleted read grant issued to their application account for the employee row's tenant.

Operations managers can read documents in their own tenant; documents from another tenant require an approved, unexpired operations document grant issued to their application user account for the document tenant, permitting read access, marked for incident response and case review, and recorded in the manager's current tenant by a grant issuer.

Finance managers can read invoices in their own tenant; invoices from another tenant require an approved, unexpired sales invoice financial-review grant issued to their application user account, permitting read access and naming an approver.
Managers and HR admins can delete archived salary history for subordinate employees only inside the current tenant and only when the salary history effective_date is older than seven years.
Finance managers can delete closed payroll rows in their department hierarchy inside the current tenant only after 90 days.
Finance managers can delete voided balance sheet entries in their region hierarchy inside the current tenant only after one year.
Finance managers can delete closed non-current bank accounts in their department hierarchy only after seven years.
DevOps engineers can delete failed builds in recursive project trees rooted at projects they own inside the current tenant only after 90 days.
Engineering managers can delete cancelled releases in recursive project trees they own inside the current tenant only when the release_date is older than 180 days.
Account managers can delete abandoned pipeline rows for customers in their recursive customer hierarchy inside the current tenant after 180 days.
Account managers can delete abandoned onboarding rows for customers in their recursive customer hierarchy inside the current tenant after one year.
Call center supervisors can delete archived recordings for recursive subordinate agents inside the current tenant only after two years.
Audit leads can delete archived audit logs for employees in their recursive reporting hierarchy inside the current tenant only after seven years.
Operations managers can delete resolved low or medium security events for recursive subordinate employees inside the current tenant only after one year.
Operations managers can delete expired documents in their department hierarchy inside the current tenant after the expiration timestamp passes.
Product managers can delete archived metrics owned by recursive subordinate employees inside the current tenant only after one year.
Data analysts can delete archived analytics owned by recursive subordinate employees inside the current tenant only after one year.
Customer support can delete duplicate resolved feedback assigned to recursive subordinate employees inside the current tenant after 30 days.
Project managers can delete archived issues in recursive project trees they own inside the current tenant only when the issue updated_at is older than 180 days.
Senior engineers can delete archived repositories in recursive project trees rooted at projects they own inside the current tenant only when the repository archived_at is older than 90 days.
Customers can delete draft unfulfilled orders for themselves or child customers in their recursive customer hierarchy inside the current tenant.
Finance managers can delete voided invoices for customers in a recursive customer hierarchy inside the current tenant only after one year.
Managers can delete stale pending attendance correction requests for recursive subordinate employees inside the current tenant after 30 days.
Finance managers can perform all row-level operations on non-archived balance sheet rows in their region hierarchy, and new or updated rows must remain in that same region hierarchy and non-archived.
Account managers can perform all operations on their own non-archived sales pipeline rows, and new or updated rows must remain assigned to them.
Call center supervisors can perform all operations on non-archived call recordings for their team, and new or updated rows must stay in that team.

Engineering managers can perform all row-level operations on planned or hotfix releases in recursive project trees rooted they own inside the current tenant, and new or updated rows must remain planned or hotfix releases in those project trees.

Finance managers can perform all row-level operations on active or pending-review bank accounts in their region hierarchy inside the current tenant, and new or updated rows must remain in that region hierarchy and tenant with an allowed account status.

Finance managers can insert pending payroll rows inside the current tenant only when the employee exists in their department hierarchy in that tenant, and the payroll row department matches that employee department.
Account managers can insert Not Started onboarding rows only for customers they manage in the current tenant.
DevOps engineers can insert queued build rows inside the current tenant only for planned or hotfix releases in recursive project trees rooted at projects they own.

Finance managers can read expense rows in their current tenant. Finance managers may update expense rows in their current tenant only when the updated row is integrity verified, transaction logged, and its approval sequence does not exceed their position level. Employees may insert their own submitted expense rows in their current tenant only when the amount is at most 5000 and a receipt is required.

Auditors, audit leads and compliance officers can read all audit logs. Only roles other than auditor and audit lead may insert or update audit log rows, and no one may write a row whose audit status is 'Audit Locked'.

Engineers can claim currently unassigned open issues in their current tenant only when the estimated hours are below 8, and the updated row must assign the issue to themselves. Project managers can insert open issues they report only for active projects they own in the current tenant.

Data analysts can read anonymized public product metrics. Product managers can update non-sensitive metrics they own in their current tenant, and the updated row must have metric status 'Validated'. Data analysts may insert metrics that include security metrics in their current tenant only when the metric is anonymized, not sensitive, and starts with metric status 'Draft'.

Sales managers can read sales contracts in their current region. Account managers may update contracts they manage only when the contract has no outstanding disputes, and the updated row must have verified payment and an approval status of Approved or Rejected. Account managers may insert contracts in their current tenant and region only when legal review and approval are required, and the discount percentage does not exceed the department discount threshold.

Application security analysts can read non-archived code repositories in their current tenant. They may insert private, branch-protected repository rows they own only for active projects in their current tenant whose required clearance does not exceed their session clearance level.
Project managers can read open pull requests they author in their current tenant. They may insert pull requests they author only with status Open, against the main, develop or release branch.
DevOps engineers can read queued build rows they triggered in their current tenant. They may insert CI, Nightly or Hotfix builds they triggered.

QA engineers can read security tests they own in their current tenant. They may insert security tests they own only when the referenced project is active and the linked issue is open in that same tenant and project.
Compliance officers can read documents they author in their current tenant and department. They may insert such documents only with a future expiration time.
Managers can read attendance rows they approved in their current tenant and department. They may insert attendance rows for employees in their recursive subordinate chain in that same department.
Employees with a recorded hire date may update their own performance records, and the updated row must remain theirs. Managers can insert submitted performance reviews for their current department.
Employees may update their own expense records in their current tenant. Finance managers may insert Submitted expense records in their current tenant.

Account managers and finance managers can update invoices they manage, but their writes cannot set the payment status to 'Archived'. Finance managers can insert new invoices only with payment status 'Paid'.

Sales representatives can update orders where they are the recorded sales rep, but their writes cannot set the fulfillment status to 'Archived'. Sales managers may insert new orders only with fulfillment status 'Pending'.
Product managers with a recorded hire date and data analysts can update metrics they own in their current tenant. Data analysts can insert Live metrics in that tenant.
Engineers can read features assigned to them in their current tenant. Product managers can delete Archived features they own in that tenant only after they have been released.

Customer support agents can update unresolved feedback assigned to them in their current tenant. Support operations staff can delete resolved feedback in that tenant only after a resolution time has been recorded.

Account managers can read customer communications for accounts they manage in their current tenant. Sales managers can insert phone communication records in that tenant only when the recorded occurrence time is not in the future.

Customer support agents with a recorded hire date can insert call recordings attributed to themselves in their current tenant only with recording status 'Recorded'. Call center supervisors can delete Archived recordings in that tenant only after they have been archived for at least 30 days.

HR specialists can read their own current salary history. HR administrators can insert their own final salary history entries only when the effective date is not in the past. HR administrators can delete their own non-current salary history only after its end date has passed.

Finance analysts can read current recognized revenue records for their department in the current tenant. Finance managers can update unrecognized revenue records in that tenant, and the updated row must be recognized with a nonnegative amount.

Compliance officers can read the audit logs in their current tenant that are still pending review. Audit leads work the same tenant's logs from the other side: they can update a log while it is not archived, leaving it closed with a recorded update time, and can create a new one only when it is an open security log.

DevOps engineers with a recorded hire date can read non-archived system configurations that require access verification in their current tenant. SREs can update configurations that are in maintenance mode in that tenant, and the updated configuration must have encryption and access verification enabled. SREs can delete archived configurations in that tenant only after their effective period has ended.

DevOps engineers can read backup records they initiated. Database administrators can approve backups, and the updated row must record them as the approver. They may delete completed backups only after the configured retention period has elapsed since the backup end time.

Engineers can read projects when they are listed as team members and their clearance meets the project's required clearance. Project managers can update projects in that tenant that have not passed the security check, and the updated row must pass the security check with at least two approvals.

HR specialists can read their own current benefit records while enrollment is open. HR administrators can insert eligible benefit records in that tenant. They may delete non-current benefit records in that tenant after coverage has ended.

Finance analysts can read tax records they own while the filing deadline has not passed. Tax specialists can update unfiled tax records in that tenant once the due date has arrived, and the updated row must record a filing time. Tax specialists can insert tax records in that tenant only when the filing date is not after the due date.

The core engineering roles hold write access to engineering issues: they can update any issue whose severity is High, Critical, or Blocker, and can delete an issue only once it is an archived duplicate assigned to them that has been inactive for more than 90 days.

Security administrators run the lifecycle of privileged temporal access records: they can create a temporary access record only after it has been approved and an access duration has been recorded, revoke an active record once a termination date is set, and delete a record that has already expired.
Sales managers can read any contract that falls inside the next 90-day renewal window, but can modify one only within the last 30 days before it expires.

Access to system configuration is gated by the clock as much as by role: employees can read configuration rows during business hours (09:00-18:00, Monday-Friday), operations managers can add disaster recovery configuration in that same window, and administrators can change an existing row only inside the 02:00-06:00 maintenance window.

Security analysts can read the security event log and resolve any event that is still unresolved inside their own tenant, but removal is kept away from them: a compliance officer is the one who deletes an event, and only once its retention window has elapsed.

HR staff can read every employee record, but only HR specialists can update one, and never their own. Deletion is held back from HR entirely: a compliance officer can purge an employee record only when it is inactive, its retention date has passed, and the employee has a recorded separation date.

Everything a product manager does to metrics stays inside their current tenant: they can read the portfolio-level metrics for portfolios they manage, update metrics that are still active, and delete archived metrics owned by employees anywhere in their recursive reporting chain once those metrics are more than a year old.

Compliance officers own the documentation side of engineering projects: they can read every privacy-critical document, create accountability-document project records under their own name, and modify the transfer impact assessment projects they own, though only during the 02:00-06:00 maintenance window.

Data analysts handle product analytics end to end within their current tenant: they can read anonymized customer analytics from the last 90 days, insert new analytics rows for that tenant, and delete archived rows owned by employees in their recursive reporting chain once those rows are more than a year old.

Auditors, working weekdays between 09:00 and 18:00, can read archived evidence audit logs and delete them once they are more than seven years old; compliance officers do the review step in between, moving logs in their current tenant from pending review to reviewed.

An expense record is created by the employee it belongs to and capped at three times that employee's currently effective monthly allowance, approved by the department manager while it is still pending and under $5000 and only inside the 02:00-06:00 maintenance window, and readable by the department's finance manager during business hours (09:00-18:00, Monday-Friday).

All payroll access is confined to the current tenant. Within it, department managers can read the exportable payroll records for their own department, while finance managers can create pending payroll rows for employees inside their department hierarchy, with the payroll row's department matching that employee's department, and can update current payroll rows so long as the row stays current.

Document permissions follow authorship and project membership: an employee can read project documents from the last 90 days when they either own the project or are listed on its team, edit a document they authored while it is still a draft less than 30 days old, and delete a contract document they authored once it has expired.

Code repository rows are guarded by clearance for reading and by ownership for writing: reading a restricted IP artifact takes clearance level 4 or higher, repository owners register repository metadata under their own name inside the current tenant, and senior engineers can delete a repository they own only after it has sat archived for at least 90 days.

Customer support employees can escalate the feedback assigned to them inside the current tenant while it is still open, and can delete a piece of feedback only when it is a duplicate that has already been resolved and was submitted within the last seven days.
Benefit records are maintained only by HR: HR specialists can create benefit enrollment rows for the active current tenant, and HR administrators can update the pension records.

Employees manage their own attendance entries: they can log their own clock-in and clock-out times, and can delete their own pending correction requests inside the current tenant on weekdays between 09:00 and 18:00, as long as the request is less than 30 days old.

Budget visibility runs down the department tree - a budget owner can read the budgets they own for their own department and every department beneath it - while changing one takes rank: a finance manager at position level 7 or higher can approve a pending increase request for their own department only when the requested increase stays within 10% of the remaining budget, and only a CFO can delete a closed department budget, only when its cycle is inactive, and only on the last day of the quarter.

Product feature rows are exposed and edited according to visibility: authenticated internal employees can read features marked public or internal; a guest user can add a feature row only when it is public, marked publicly visible, and created on a weekday between 09:00 and 18:00; and product managers can update active features inside the current tenant.

Sales managers can read the customers in their assigned region that have been contacted within the last 90 days, and can delete an inactive customer only on a weekday between 09:00 and 18:00, and only when that customer has gone more than three years without contact and holds no active contract.
QA engineers can read the test results for the products they own, and can approve the release QA records assigned to them except where they are also the assigned developer.

Procurement officers run the order pipeline: they can read orders that are pending fulfillment, raise new orders in that same pending state for their current tenant, and approve or reject a pending purchase order only when its amount stays within 10000 times their position level.

Accountants can read the invoices that are pending payment and update the payment status on verified invoices, though only inside the 02:00-06:00 maintenance window. Deleting an invoice is reserved for finance managers, and only while it is still a draft in their current tenant.

Finance analysts can read quarterly revenue records whose report period is on or before today and can add new revenue rows only for the active current tenant, so nothing is booked forward and nothing crosses tenants. Removing a record is a finance manager's call, limited to voided reports marked as corrections and only after the revenue row has been closed.
Tax specialists can read only the current year's tax records, and the only rows they can delete are drafts inside their current tenant.

Department managers can read every performance review in their department, but editing belongs to the assigned reviewer, who can change a review only while it is in draft status and must leave it in draft.

Call center supervisors own their team's recordings inside the current tenant: they can read the recordings belonging to their team, move a recording from recorded to reviewed, and delete archived recordings belonging to agents anywhere in their recursive reporting chain once those recordings are more than two years old.

Backup records are read by clearance and written by role: a user at security clearance level 4 or higher can read backup rows during business hours (09:00-18:00, Monday-Friday), build administrators restore approved backups only inside the 02:00-06:00 maintenance window and must leave the row with a restored timestamp and a backup status of Restored, and security administrators delete a backup record once its retention period has expired.

Strategic roadmap material is gated by seniority on both sides: reading a strategic plan row takes clearance level 5 or higher, and adding a strategic roadmap item to the current tenant takes position level 7 or higher. Roadmap owners can delete only their own items, and only after those items have been deferred, within their tenant.

DevOps engineers can write build rows only within the recursive project trees rooted at projects they own inside the current tenant: there they can queue a new build for a planned or hotfix release, and can delete a failed build once it is more than 90 days old.

Account managers run customer onboarding inside the current tenant: they can open a record in the Not Started state for a customer they manage, update the in-progress records assigned to them, and delete an abandoned record for a customer anywhere in their recursive customer hierarchy once it is more than a year old.

Account managers can read the communication history for the accounts they manage during business hours (09:00-18:00, Monday-Friday), and can close a pending communication record for one of those accounts inside the current tenant.
